title: Release handoff compact and variant sprint folio — 2028-06 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact handoff folio for the week-of release that stitches together the rollout calendar, short checklists for on-call and release owners, and a draft of release notes to hand to Customer Success and Documentation teams. Treat as living: add quick observations during the watch window in the NOTES section.

High-level target:
- Ship: model routing adjustments + batching config tweaks + small config for autoscaler (no schema changes).
- Goal: roll to 10% traffic in cohort A -> monitor 24h -> expand to 50% -> final ramp to 100% over 72h if signals green.

Quick decision matrix (owner initials):
- Go/no-go 0h after canary smoke: Release Lead (JL) with SRE (EC) and Product (MK).
- Rollback threshold: >1.5x baseline p95 latency OR >2% error-rate delta sustained for 15m. Decision = immediate rollback.
- Fallback plan: route cohort A traffic to previous model variant (variant-v2) via routing-flag. Ops owner: Priya.

Compact preflight checklist (T-24h to T-1h):
- Code/infra:
  - Confirm PRs merged and CI green (PR #459) — JL.
  - Verify infra templates staged in canary env — EC.
  - Confirm autoscaler policy change is a patch-only config (no DB migrations) — SP.
- Observability:
  - Grafana dashboard slate for this rollout created and pinned (latency p50/p95, errors, token throughput) — MK.
  - Tracing span to instrument new routing path enabled — EC.
  - Alert blast test: run blast to ensure alerting recipients correct — JL.
- Communication:
  - Release notes draft shared with CS + Docs (link below) — JL.
  - Slack channel #release-handovers created and all watchers invited — JL.
- Safety:
  - Canary abort switch validated and accessible via ops console — Priya.
  - Rollback playbook verified (route revert + scale down new machines) — EC.

Rollout calendar (text timeline):
- Day 0, 10:00 UTC: Deploy artifacts to canary pool (10 nodes). Smoke deploy run (10m).
- Day 0, 10:15 UTC: Start cohort A (1% traffic ramp) -> 1h watch.
- Day 0, 11:30 UTC: If stable, bump cohort A -> 10% traffic. 24h watch.
- Day 1, 12:00 UTC: If green, expand to cohort B -> 50% traffic. 12h watch.
- Day 2, 00:00-06:00 UTC: Analyze cost/latency tradeoffs; final step to 100% if signals ok.
Notes: schedule windows chosen to avoid our peak APAC usage; adjust if partner-reported traffic shifts.

Canary smoke checklist (Day 0 10:00):
- Sanity queries: 20 sample requests across short/long sequences, ensure expected token consumption and KV cache hits.
- End-to-end latency check: compare to baseline synthetic workload.
- Error surface: ensure no new 5xx patterns in route logs.
- Model output sanity: spot-check 10 responses for regressions (product SME to confirm).

Metrics to monitor (owner):
- p50/p95 latency (EC), p99 if significant traffic (EC).
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) and error classes (JL).
- Token throughput and billing token delta (MK).
- Model quality signals: small eval prompt set A/B (Product) — samples per hour.
- Autoscaler scale events and backpressure signs (EC).

Rollback and mitigation steps (quick):
1) Abort ramp flag -> freeze traffic.
2) Re-route to variant-v2 via routing API (Priya).
3) Scale down new pool and validate old pool healthy (EC).
4) Postmortem checklist kick-off and preserve traces/logs (JL).

Post-rollout checks (first 24h):
- Cost telemetry: review token unit cost delta vs baseline (MK).
- Quality sampling: Product to run full prompt set and log any drift (Marta).
- Customer impact: CS to watch for incoming tickets and log concerns (linked doc).

Draft release notes (shareable summary for Docs/CS):
- Summary: small runtime change to routing and batching configuration intended to reduce per-token tail latency and improve throughput for medium-length sequences. No model weight changes.
- What changed: updated routing policy to prefer packed-batches for medium sequences; small autoscaler policy tweak to reduce scale-up oscillation.
- Why: measurably better p95 in internal benchmarks for our typical workloads and lower cost-per-token for mid-range requests.
- Impact: expect ~5–12% p95 latency reduction on serving-runtime for requests with 128–512 tokens; potential small uptick in CPU usage during packing window.
- Rollout plan: staged canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72h with rollback thresholds and automatic abort.
- Known risks: potential for transient errors during initial packing ramp; we have a fast rollback path.
- Contact: release lead Jordan Lee, SRE on-call Evan Chen, Product owner Marta Korhonen.

Operator quick-reference (for watch shifts):
- Triage first: are errors correlated to model-routing path? Check request header X-Route and routing logs.
- If >1.5x p95: hit abort flag, notify release lead.
- If errors spike but latency fine: throttle cohort expansion and kick off deeper log tail analysis.

NOTES (live, add observations here):
- 2028-06-05 09:22 JL: PR green but one flaky test in integration: test/autoscale/scale_down.test — flagged for debug.
- 2028-06-06 14:05 EC: Dashboard added; need to add token billing metric to main pinboard.
- 2028-06-07 07:12 MK: Customer pilot (acct: BrightWell) scheduled—advise delaying final ramp to avoid noise.

Open questions / followups:
- Do we want service-level canaries per-region or a single global cohort? (tradeoffs: more signal isolation vs complexity). Owner: JL
- Confirm Docs wording for "no model change" message; Product to draft exact phrasing. Owner: MK
- Validate whether AVX-512 optimized kernel gets invoked in dedicated pool; infra follow-up required (EC).

Postmortem template (if rollback):
- Timeline log + exact metric deltas (attach dashboard snapshots).
- Root cause hypothesis and immediate remediation.
- Longer-term action items and owner assignments.

Appendix - quick links (placeholders):
- Release artifacts: build-2028-06-05-459
- Routing flag: feature/route-variant-2028-06
- Ops console runbook: confluence/ops/rollback-playbook

End of folio. Add short notes to this doc during watch; we'll fold into the full release retrospective after 48h.
